_comment: Brackets confirmed against CRA. Ontario has NOT published its 2026 package,
so every amount below is estimated from the 2025 figure — which is itself now
verified against ON428 — indexed at Ontario's own 1.9% factor, derived from
the confirmed brackets (53,891 / 52,886). The federal 2.0% does not apply.
Replace these when Ontario publishes, around January 2027.

income_tax.source: VERIFIED 2026-08-16 against CRA, Current year tax rates and income brackets 2026 (canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/individuals/tax-rates-brackets/current-year.html). Thresholds and rates both confirmed.

credit_rate.source: VERIFIED 2026-08-16 against CRA/Ontario Ministry of Finance, Form ON428 2025 (5006-C) and Worksheet ON428 (5006-D) for 2025; statutory rate, unchanged for 2026.

bpa.source: Ontario basic personal amount for 2026. CRA, T4032-ON Payroll Deductions Tables, January 2026 (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/forms-publications/payroll/t4032-payroll-deductions-tables/t4032on-jan/t4032on-january-general-information.html). Checked 2026-09-15.

care_rate_base_tier1.source: Schedule ON479-A: 75% of the federal child care deduction for family income up to $20,000.

care_tier1_ceiling.source: Schedule ON479-A: the full 75% rate applies up to $20,000 of family income.

care_rate_base_tier2.source: Schedule ON479-A: the second tier also starts at 75%, reduced by 2% for each $2,500 (or part) of income above $20,000.

care_tier2_ceiling.source: Schedule ON479-A: second tier runs to $40,000.

care_tier2_step.source: Schedule ON479-A: $2,500 income step in the second tier, counting each part-step as a whole one.

care_rate_base_tier3.source: Schedule ON479-A: 59% base for the $40,000-$60,000 tier. Corroborated by Ontario's own worked example: at $45,500 the rate is 55%, which is 59% - 2% x ceil(5500/5000) = 59% - 4%.

care_tier3_ceiling.source: Schedule ON479-A: third tier runs to $60,000.

care_tier3_step.source: Schedule ON479-A: $5,000 income step in the third tier. Confirmed by Ontario's worked example at $45,500.

care_rate_base_tier4.source: Schedule ON479-A: 51% base for the $60,000-$150,000 tier, reduced by 2% for each $3,600 (or part) above $60,000, reaching zero at $150,000.

care_tier4_ceiling.source: Schedule ON479-A: the credit reaches zero at $150,000 of family income.

care_tier4_step.source: Schedule ON479-A: $3,600 income step in the fourth tier, which takes 51% to zero across the $60,000-$150,000 range in 25 steps.

care_step_reduction.source: Schedule ON479-A: every step reduces the rate by 2 percentage points.

age_amount_max.source: ESTIMATED, NOT PUBLISHED. The verified 2025 figure indexed at Ontario's 2026 factor of 1.9%, which is itself now confirmed against CRA's T4032-ON (checked 2026-09-15). Every estimate in this pack that could be checked against a published 2026 figure proved correct, with one exception — the tax reduction per dependant, which Ontario raised rather than indexed. That is why this stays unverified: the method is sound and a legislature is still free to do something else. A T1 return must not be filed on it. (Amount: 6341.)

tuition_transfer_max.source: Ontario abolished the tuition and education tax credits for studies after 5 September 2017 (Taxation Act, 2007 amendments). There is no Ontario current-year tuition transfer, so the maximum is nil. The federal transfer under ITA s.118.81 is unaffected.
